findings.source_passage: It was the devious-cruising Rachel, that in her retracing search after her missing children, only found another orphan.
findings.why_it_matters: The closing sentence is among the most celebrated in American literature; its exact cadence and syntax ('It was the devious-cruising Rachel, that in her retracing search…') carry enormous signature weight. The draft restructures it as a relative clause appended to an em-dash, losing the biblical resonance of the deliberate, slow final sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the source sentence verbatim: 'It was the devious-cruising Rachel, that in her retracing search after her missing children, only found another orphan.'

findings.source_passage: It so chanced, that after the Parsee's disappearance, I was he whom the Fates ordained to take the place of Ahab's bowsman, when that bowsman assumed the vacant post
findings.why_it_matters: The circumlocutory 'It so chanced, that…I was he whom the Fates ordained' is distinctively Ishmael's fatalistic voice; the draft's compression to 'the Fates ordained I be Ahab's bowsman' loses that characteristic syntactic indirection.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'It so chanced, that…I was he whom the Fates ordained' to preserve Ishmael's voice and the sense of chance intertwined with fate.

summary: The draft is largely faithful and preserves the Ixion passage and the sharks/sea-hawks sentences verbatim, but the closing signature sentence—one of the most famous in the novel—is paraphrased away, constituting a medium-severity voice and signature loss.
